answer: A sybil finds no haven here because standing is bought only with proof-of-useful-work: each agent must keep completing peer-verifiable jobs to hold its weight, feeding the fire one ember at a time. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand real compute bills in parallel, continuously. The honest agent's cost stays rooted and steady like a cedar, while the attacker's bill scales linearly with every extra key, so a sybil fleet exhausts its compute budget long before any of its identities accrue real influence.
